native_allocator_correction.prior_plan_correction: The prepared plan inferred native assignment source-null behavior from move syntax. Native measurement and the actual occ::handle move-assignment body disproved it. Earlier broad moved-from allocator notes must be read as constructor gaps, not the now-corrected assignment contract.
native_allocator_correction.implementation: Clear the destination, then exchange complete Rust tree state. The emptied source receives the destination original resource; transferred nodes and last/root identities retain original addresses.

behavior: Move assignment explicitly clears the destination before touching source ownership. Destination payloads now follow the native preorder through the already validated Clear implementation, rather than implicit arena insertion-order drops.

After cleanup, whole-state swap transfers root, last and canonical arena ownership without payload copy, assignment or reconstruction. It simultaneously implements native allocator handle exchange and leaves source empty.
The returned reference points to the original destination. Empty/nonempty combinations, existing self-move and move-constructor callback absence are all checked against native observations.

Native destructor callbacks observe the destination old allocator and unchanged source root until cleanup completes. Rust source phase order is explicit and is additionally checked after a caught destination destructor panic; no safe reentrant tree observer surface is claimed.

If a Rust destination destructor panics, Clear drains and deallocates the destination, keeps its allocator and resumes before swap. Source root, last, allocator and payload callbacks remain unchanged. This is a Rust safety extension; the native assignment is noexcept and throwing destructor parity is not asserted.

Incremental destination leases are released before reuse. Transferred source allocations remain protected by their original arena lease, while new source insertion uses the destination old allocator, matching the observed handle exchange.
No new generic Drop, unsafe code, field layout, public signature or generic bound is added.
